headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty plunged over 1% dragged down by private banking and IT stocks

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Wednesday, 21 October.

why: Heavy selling in private banking and IT stocks dragged benchmark indices down in the last session.
Elevated crude oil prices weighed on investor sentiment and broadened market losses.
Investors lost over ₹4 lakh crore as market capitalization eroded during Monday's crash.
Global tech stock weakness and market volatility contributed to domestic market decline.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets are closed today, 20 October 2026, due to an NSE trading holiday.
In the last session, Sensex fell 876 points while Nifty dropped 1.11% in a sharp market sell-off.
Jio Platforms drew a record ₹2.5 lakh crore in anchor bids ahead of its IPO.
The RBI injected ₹1 lakh crore into the banking system to ease liquidity tightness ahead of the festive season.
summary:
Indian stock markets are closed today due to an NSE holiday and will reopen on Wednesday, 21 October.
In the last trading session, Sensex and Nifty slumped over 1% as private banks, IT stocks, and rising crude oil prices triggered a market-wide sell-off.
Major corporate updates include record anchor bids for Jio Platforms' IPO and strong brokerage backing for ICICI Bank following its Q2 earnings.
